name: Citizenship restoration under Article 116(2) Basic Law

requirements.blocker_text: This requires being a former German citizen deprived of citizenship on political, racial, or religious grounds between 30 January 1933 and 8 May 1945, or a descendant of such a person — all generations qualify, and each descendant has an individual claim following the 2020 Federal Constitutional Court ruling (2 BvR 2628/18).

evidence_required.document: Documentation of the ancestor's deprivation of German citizenship and the persecution basis
Full documented descent chain from the ancestor to the applicant

sources.title: Bundesverwaltungsamt - Article 116(2) Basic Law citizenship restoration

notes: Direct structural equivalent to uk_ancestry, but fundamentally different in mechanism — this is a citizenship ENTITLEMENT (Anspruch) restoring what was wrongfully taken, not a route someone qualifies into via bloodline the way UK Ancestry's grandparent test works. No residence requirement, no language requirement, no naturalisation test, and — genuinely unusual across this entire dataset — free of charge. citizenship_after_months is 0 because this route GRANTS citizenship directly rather than leading to it, structurally identical to how uk_citizenship itself has citizenship_after_months: 0. All generations of descendants qualify with an individual claim (not just one generation, unlike UK Ancestry's single-grandparent-generation test) — confirmed via the 2020 Constitutional Court ruling expanding the original interpretation. A related but distinct route, §15 StAG (restitution), covers cases falling outside Article 116(2) — not encoded as a separate route here, flagged as a scope decision.
